title: Hybrid burst autoscaler with cost-watermarking and soft-fence controls
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement a hybrid burst autoscaling policy for Dedicated fleets that combines predictive headroom, reactive surge pools, and a cost-watermarking signal to shape temporary boosts. The feature should provide soft-fence controls so we can accept short bursts without immediate hard preemption while limiting long-run overage exposure. Goals: 1) let tenants absorb short traffic spikes from the burst pool with predictable latency SLOs, 2) throttle or redirect sustained bursts to avoid surprise overage billing, 3) expose tenant-facing signals (watermark, remaining-burst-credit, estimated-invoice-impact) in Console and billing UI. This ticket covers API, controller logic, and operator runbook for initial rollout to a subset of Dedicated clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Autoscaler implements hybrid policy combining: predictive headroom (short-term forecast), reactive surge allocation, and cost-watermarking threshold that degrades burst allocation when expected overage exceeds watermark.

Soft-fence behavior: bursts under 10 minutes are allowed to continue with degraded fairness but not preempted; bursts over 30 minutes trigger progressive throttling and fallback routing to lower-cost model variants or queueing.
Expose metrics: surge_allocated_tokens, cost_watermark_percent, burst_credit_remaining, burst_estimated_overage_usd. Metrics are visible in Console per-fleet and exported to Datadog.
Billing simulation dashboard shows invoice shaping for test tenants: baseline vs hybrid-autoscaler enabled vs hard-fence baseline, with 95th percentile invoice delta under control.
E2E tests that simulate short spikes, sustained spikes, and oscillating traffic, validating SLOs and invoice estimates. Tests pass in CI and as a canary in prod cluster alpha-dedicated-03.
Operator runbook added to Confluence with playbook steps, rollback criteria, and links to related PRs/alerts.
Feature gated behind runtime flag and rollout plan allowing per-tenant opt-in and a default conservative watermark for public tenants.

2026-03-12 Aisha Kapoor: Follow-ups: (1) finalize watermark bias factor, (2) add dashboard tile for 'burst_estimated_overage_usd' per-tenant, (3) add integration test for billing export pipeline. Assigned to ENG-748901 for billing export work.
implementation_notes: Key components: 1) Predictive headroom service (golang) using short-window AR forecasting; 2) Burst allocator using gradient-based fairness that respects tenant priority; 3) Cost-watermarker computes a rolling expected-overage USD and compares to tenant watermark; 4) Soft-fence implements progressive throttles and fallback routing to pinned lower-cost model variants. Keep logic idempotent and tolerant to controller restarts. Use leader-election per-fleet controller.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Watermark miscalibration could either block legitimate short spikes or allow runaway overage. Mitigation: conservative bias factor, per-tenant opt-in, phased rollout, and realtime billing alerting.
Risk: Allocation churn under oscillating traffic. Mitigation: add allocation dampening timer and hysteresis (implemented in prototype).
Risk: Billing pipeline lag causing mismatch in estimated vs actual invoice. Mitigation: tag estimates as provisional and include margin; coordinate with ENG-748901 to shorten export lag.
